record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.context_brief: open subspaces of CDH metric spaces
record.original_question: If X is a countable dense homogeneous metric space and U is an open subspace of X, must U itself be countable dense homogeneous?

evidence.quote: Problem 2. If X is CDH and metric and U is open in X, must U be CDH?
Problem 2 and the first part of Problem 2’ were answered by van Mill [67]: there is a CDH Polish space with a dense connected open subset that is rigid.

artifact.self_contained_problem: A topological space $X$ is called countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for any two countable dense subsets $D_1, D_2 \subseteq X$ there exists a homeomorphism $h\colon X \to X$ with $h(D_1) = D_2$. Suppose $X$ is a metrizable CDH space and $U \subseteq X$ is a (nonempty) open subspace of $X$. Must $U$, with the subspace topology, also be countable dense homogeneous?
artifact.status_search_result: The question was answered negatively by J. van Mill, who constructed a Polish (hence metric) CDH space containing a dense connected open subset that is rigid (its only self-homeomorphism is the identity), and so in particular is not CDH. Thus open subspaces of metric CDH spaces need not be CDH.

status_evidence.title: Open subspaces of countable dense homogeneous spaces (J. van Mill)
status_evidence.snippet: There is a CDH-space X containing a dense connected rigid open subset; this example is Polish.
status_evidence.claim: Van Mill produced a Polish CDH space with a dense rigid open subspace, so open subspaces of metric CDH spaces need not be CDH.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 2 was answered by van Mill: there is a CDH Polish space with a dense connected open subset that is rigid.
status_evidence.claim: Survey records that the problem was solved by van Mill in the negative.
